alerts.title: DTG-associated weight gain and metabolic syndrome
alerts.message: Guidelines state weight gain should be discussed when starting all ART regimens, with proactive diet and exercise advice, as obesity is an increasing problem particularly among women. Patient gained 17kg (65→82kg) and BMI rose from 25.6→32.4 within 18 months of switching to DTG. Acanthosis nigricans, elevated BP (138/88), impaired fasting glucose (118 mg/dL), pre-diabetic HbA1c (6.1%), and dyslipidemia now present. DTG is strongly associated with weight gain; switching from EFV may have unmasked weight gain previously suppressed by EFV. Family history of Type 2 Diabetes compounds risk. Non-drug contributors include diet and physical inactivity. No clinician assessment or plan was documented today.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide diet and exercise counselling. Consider glucose monitoring every 3 months. Evaluate for diabetes intervention. Document assessment and management plan.

alerts.title: Missing DTG glucose monitoring per guideline
alerts.message: Guidelines specify glucose monitoring every 3 months for the first year when transitioning to DTG. Patient transitioned to DTG 18 months ago; no record of quarterly glucose monitoring exists in available data. Current fasting glucose is 118 mg/dL (impaired) and HbA1c 6.1% (pre-diabetic), confirming that glucose dysregulation has developed. The monitoring gap means deterioration may have gone undetected earlier. Family history of Type 2 Diabetes further increases risk.

evidence.recommended_action: Initiate regular glucose and HbA1c monitoring at least every 3-6 months given pre-diabetic status and ongoing DTG use.

alerts.title: No assessment or plan documented for abnormal findings
alerts.message: Patient presents with significant weight gain (17kg in 18 months), new hypertension-range BP (138/88 mmHg), impaired fasting glucose, pre-diabetic HbA1c, and atherogenic dyslipidemia (LDL 148, HDL 38, triglycerides 212). No clinician assessment or plan was documented for this visit. Guidelines emphasise proactive management of weight gain including diet and exercise advice. The combination of obesity, pre-diabetes, hypertension, and dyslipidemia constitutes metabolic syndrome requiring coordinated intervention.

evidence.recommended_action: Document assessment addressing weight gain, BP, glucose, and lipids. Initiate lifestyle counselling and pharmacologic intervention as indicated.
